title: Function dispatch regression harness: evaluate selection accuracy & argument validation across config/model changes
creator: Ayesha Malik
description: Build a reproducible eval harness that continuously measures tool/function dispatch accuracy and argument validation correctness against model and configuration changes. The harness should exercise the function-calling surface across model variants, quantization profiles, routing policies, and serving configs (batching, sampling). Goals: detect quality regressions early in PRs and deploy pipelines, provide clear delta metrics, and wire alerts to the Console/Slack when thresholds are exceeded.
acceptance_criteria: A baseline benchmark dataset (>= 1.5k examples) covering selection edge-cases, ambiguous prompts, and argument-boundary cases is checked into evals repo
Harness executes permutations: model variant, quantization (fp16/int8), sampling (temp/top_p), routing policy (primary/fallback), and batching config — and records metric deltas

Metrics produced: tool selection accuracy, top-2 containment, argument schema validation rate, malformed-arg rate, semantic-arg-fidelity score (BLEU/EM or custom), latency distribution; stored per-run and per-commit
CI gate configured: any >4% absolute regression in tool selection accuracy or >3% increase in malformed-arg rate across a PR fails the job
Dashboard in Console with historical trends and an alert channel (Slack #eng-regressions + PagerDuty playbook) for high-severity regressions
Playbook documented with triage steps and links to the failing examples + suggested mitigations (prompt tuning, model pinning, fallback policy adjustments)

design_decisions: Use dataset-driven deterministic examples rather than purely synthetic generation to ensure reproducibility and debuggability
Store per-example seeds and runtime configs to enable exact replay of failing cases
Run full permutation matrix in nightly job; run a prioritized subset (highest-risk permutations) in PR/merge CI to keep latency practical
Metric thresholds are absolute (percentage points) instead of relative to avoid noise sensitivity across low-frequency tools
Expose per-config baselines so teams can pin to a known-good config if a model variant introduces regressions
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: combinatorial explosion of permutations causes long run times — Mitigation: prioritize permutations using historical traffic heatmap and a risk score; use sampling for rare combos
Risk: noisy metrics from stochastic sampling (temp/top_p) — Mitigation: run N seeds per config and report mean+CI; use deterministic seeds for replay
Risk: false positives due to dataset bias — Mitigation: maintain holdout and adversarial subsets; rotate periodic data refresh
Risk: sensitive customer data in example traces — Mitigation: sanitize PII and enforce retention policies; restrict access to eval artifacts
